sss.issuance: SSS Circular No. 2024-006, Schedule of SSS Contributions effective January 2025 (RA 11199)
notes: Compensation below ₱5,250 uses the ₱5,000 minimum Monthly Salary Credit; ₱34,750 and over uses the ₱35,000 maximum.
The employee pays 5% of the MSC: Regular SS on the first ₱20,000 and the Mandatory Provident Fund on the rest.
Employer share (10%) and Employees' Compensation (₱10/₱30) are paid by the employer and are not deducted from pay.
2025 was the last scheduled increase under RA 11199; the SSS page lists this schedule as current.

philhealth.issuance: PhilHealth Circular No. 2020-0005 premium schedule (RA 11223, Universal Health Care Act): 5% from 2024
notes: Premium is 5% of monthly basic salary, floored at ₱10,000 and capped at ₱100,000, shared equally by employer and employee.
The official circular is a scanned document; figures were cross-checked against multiple payroll references.

pagibig.issuance: HDMF Circular No. 460: maximum Monthly Fund Salary raised to ₱10,000
notes: Employee share: 1% of monthly compensation up to ₱1,500, 2% above that, computed on at most ₱10,000 (₱200 maximum).
Members may voluntarily contribute more; only the mandatory share is excluded from taxable income here.
pagibigfund.gov.ph blocks automated access; figures were cross-checked against multiple payroll references.

tax.issuance: RR No. 11-2018 (TRAIN, RA 10963): graduated rates for 2023 onwards and Annex E withholding tables
notes: Taxable compensation excludes mandatory employee SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG contributions and union dues.
13th month pay and other benefits are exempt up to ₱90,000 a year; the excess is taxable.
Statutory minimum wage earners are exempt on their minimum wage, holiday, overtime, night differential and hazard pay.
Biweekly pay is not covered by Annex E; this calculator applies the weekly table to each week (half the biweekly pay).
